item.title: Patching php2shell in My Alpine Lighttpd PHP Docker Image
item.description:
If you use my alpine-lighttpd-php Docker image, please pull :latest again and recreate your container. The image now runs PHP 8.4.27, which fixes the php2shell vulnerabilities.

docker pull alastairhm/alpine-lighttpd-php:latest
# or
docker pull ghcr.io/alastairhm/alpine-lighttpd-php:latest

What is php2shell?

php2shell is the name for two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Both are critical, and both allow remote code execution with no authentication. PHP published a security advisory on 21 October, alongside fixed releases 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.

item.title: New Posts Now Announce Themselves on Bluesky
item.description:
New posts on this blog now get announced on Bluesky automatically, alongside the Mastodon toots that were already going out. If you’re reading this via a Bluesky link card, that’s the thing working.

It went live on 16 October, with the Inktober “Gangly” post being the first one through, and it’s been quietly doing its job since.

How it works

The whole thing is a GitHub Actions workflow plus a small Python script, with no third-party service in the middle.
